sentences.text: Mandrasuchus is an extinct genus of alligatorine, a type of crocodilian, recovered as a member of the subfamily Alligatorinae. The holotype, which is the specimen the species is based on, is DMNH EPV.48541 and includes parts of the skull, tail, armor plates, and limbs.

This animal reached about 2 meters in length, slightly smaller than the 2.3-meter Borealosuchus specimens found nearby. Its varied teeth suggest it was a macro-generalist predator capable of eating large prey and crushing the shells of molluscs, crustaceans, and turtles.

The species name milleri honors Ian Miller, who discovered many specimens at the Denver Museum of Nature & Science. Fossils of Mandrasuchus have been found in Colorado, United States, specifically within the Denver Formation.
Mandrasuchus lived during the Danian stage of the Paleocene, appearing within the first million years after the K-Pg event. It is the oldest confirmed alligatorine from this time period.
It is debated whether teeth and osteoderms found near the K-Pg boundary in Weld County belong to Mandrasuchus, as similar dentition exists in Late Cretaceous crocodilians.
